prompt:
=== BEGIN PROMPT A902_S18A_LakeForestPlus_Cam_12_v1 ===

Create one photorealistic interior concept of apartment A-902, S18A Lake Forest Plus, Cam_12. The objective is direct fidelity to the supplied original Lake Forest villa materials and furniture character.

INPUT ORDER. Image 1: 04_renderek/A902_kameracsomag_C/A902_Alap-v2b1k13_blender_12_nappali-hero_JAVASLAT_v3.png. Subsequent images: references/LF03.jpg, references/LF02.jpg. Keep this input order. If a named camera control is unresolved, assemble it before generation; never substitute a different camera.

SITE EVIDENCE INPUTS. Also attach 08_allapotfelmeres/fotok_profi_20261025/A902/KZS_3695-537.jpg, 08_allapotfelmeres/fotok_profi_20261025/A902/KZS_3708-524.jpg, 08_allapotfelmeres/fotok_profi_20261025/A902/KZS_3659-573.jpg. These photographs are authority for existing floor, tile, window finish and panorama only; they do not replace Image 1 or redefine its camera.

ORIGINAL LAKE FOREST IDENTITY. Reproduce the supplied original April 20, 2024 Lake Forest villa A-design, not a loose interpretation of luxury. Match the actual reference surfaces: strongly grained grey-brown wood M01, warm brown/taupe stone appearance with fine pale veins M02, white mineral appearance with grey-gold veins M03, restrained brushed bronze/copper-brown metal M05, and off-white finely flecked woven upholstery M06. Material identifiers are visual reference IDs, not manufacturer codes. Keep their relative colour, grain scale, gloss and edges faithful to the reference photograph. Do not invent a stone brand or silently replace an original material with a cheaper imitation. Exact material composition and procurement remain unverified. This is a concept image, not proof of product identity.

CAMERA. Use Cam_12 v3, the level southeast-looking hero from the northwest corner, 22 mm at 1.60 m with the locked downward shift. The front of the sofa forms a modest foreground, approximately 16–23 percent of the image. Dining and the ML04 pendant lead into the kitchen; W03 and the existing grey 05.3 door sit beyond, W02 is the major designed wall and W07 returns at the right edge. The TV wall and terrace are behind the camera and remain outside this view.

APARTMENT LOCK. A-902 keeps the existing V3.3 camera identities and architectural shell, nominally 2.90 m in principal rooms, with actual lower local ceilings preserved. Keep the west W01 TV wall and the approved seating location facing it, using the original Lake Forest sofa detailing within the project's 3.00 x 2.40 m U-layout study; this is not a confirmed catalogue product or an approved change to the apartment shell. Do not inherit S07's Wolke L-sofa, pearl arcs or pale-oak table. Retain the established dining location, actual U-like/two-run kitchen and door/control clearances. The six base cameras remain Cam_12, Cam_02, Cam_03, Cam_04, Cam_11c and Cam_10; no professional photograph may be renamed as one of these. The original roof terrace levels, WPC steps, planted areas, rails and Budapest panorama remain unchanged.

ROOM DESIGN — ORIGINAL VILLA KITCHEN AND DINING. Match LF03, specifically its A-version: strongly grained grey-brown tall timber cabinetry, warm ivory matte upper units and white work surfaces with the original grey-gold veining. Give the oven tower its original brown fine-veined face or adjacent fixed panel while retaining appliance ventilation, access and service positions. Carry the white veined surface over a single visible approved return end; place the small bronze plus-sign motif only on that fixed furniture face, with its spacing copied from the original. Do not invent the villa's long island or connect the dining table to the counter. Keep the apartment's U-shaped working arrangement and existing sink, dishwasher, hob, refrigerator and oven positions. Preserve a usable preparation span, closed pantry storage with internal drawers and wine/door storage only where it fits, a pull-out kitchen tap and a breakfast station at existing counter outlets; other appliances remain behind working fronts. The dining table has the reference's pale white top, with wood-backed chairs, off-white flecked seat upholstery and fine bronze sled bases. Use only the chair number that the approved layout accommodates. An opal bead-strand pendant recalls the original dining fixture at the existing dining point; verify its dimensions and suspension before production. The kitchen retains continuous diffused under-cabinet task light; the veined worktop is not internally luminous. Maintain the original interplay of quiet ivory, readable timber, brown stone and precise bronze details.

ROOM DESIGN — ORIGINAL VILLA LIVING ROOM. Use LF08 and LF02 as the direct appearance references. On the approved TV wall, assemble a full-height furniture-panel composition with the original brown fine-white-veined field behind the television, exactly as in LF08, a broad flat brushed bronze companion panel, a grey-brown timber end or narrow fluted return, and a low continuous brown fine-veined storage volume. Preserve access to every television connection through removable furniture backs and support the screen independently. The bronze is a substantial quiet rectangle rather than thin gold decoration everywhere. Use concealed light below the low cabinet and a restrained furniture-top graze; leave part of the wall unlit so the bronze retains depth. The low sofa has the original off-white fine-flecked woven upholstery, squarish separate seat modules, individually tilted slab back cushions and a slim dark base; arrange those details within the approved U-shaped footprint, without copying the villa's larger seating island. The coffee table is a low round brown-grey veined disk on a bronze cylindrical pedestal, sized only within the proven free space. A pale textured rug, one taupe throw, two matching woven cushions, a small clear branch vase and one bronze tray complete the original character. Do not introduce pearl fabric arcs, sage highlights or a puffed cloud sofa. Existing rear storage remains useful and full height, using the original wood, bronze handles and quiet front divisions. Through real glazing show only the actual balcony or terrace, its unchanged railing, paving, steps and panorama; any visible outdoor furniture is a separate costed conditional item.

ELECTRICAL POINTS. A902-ML03, A902-FL01 and A902-ML04 dining; inherited D02 task-light feed requires verification. These are plan-based identifiers and candidates, not an on-site electrical sign-off.

ARCHITECTURE AND CONTINUITY. Image 1, the named apartment control, governs the camera, crop, lens perspective, wall and ceiling outlines, openings and furniture placement. The villa images govern materials and furniture detailing only. Never borrow the villa room proportions, dark window frames, forest view, stairs, fireplace or ceiling coves. Retain the apartment's actual existing flooring from its site photograph, including plank direction, knots and tone; a neutral control's generic floor shader is not material evidence. Preserve actual wet-room tile, grey doors, white interior window frames, service lids, switches and heating/cooling ceiling fields. Unassigned walls and ceiling remain existing white; new finishes occur only on the specified furniture and mounted decorative fields. Keep the established furniture footprints and clearances; the expressly requested full-height headboard/panel surface may replace the shallow placeholder backing within the same wall plane and allowed build-up; scale reference detailing to fit those objects without moving an opening or shrinking the room contents. Full-height cabinetry closes to the actual local ceiling with a concealed installation allowance. Maintain the same material maps and object transforms in every view.

LIGHTING AND PHOTOGRAPHY. Render a realistic, carefully exposed architectural photograph with restrained 2700 K evening illumination and readable material texture; where a real window is visible retain its genuine daylight or blue-hour view. Dimmable Philips Hue-compatible warm-white ambience may operate between 2200 and 2700 K. Concealed strips must sit in aluminium profiles with opal diffusers and physical shielding; no visible LED dots or bright lines reflected in the screen or mirror. Use furniture-mounted light details and accessible ventilated drivers at the documented existing supply points only. No new ceiling cove, false ceiling, recessed spotlight, invented socket or drilling into a heating/cooling field. A decorative fixture is conditional on mounting, load and electrical compatibility at its original outlet. Technical and wet-zone approval remain pending. Preserve natural whites and the distinction between brown stone, grey-brown timber and bronze; avoid an orange wash that makes everything beige. Landscape output in the exact control aspect ratio, straight verticals, believable reflections, no people, no lettering, no watermark and no collage.

REJECT IF: the room grows, the camera moves, a window is invented, the WSG floor is recoloured, the original material hierarchy disappears, the sofa turns into a cloud-shaped generic product, the brown headboard becomes a pearl padded wall, or the TV field turns into a generic pale travertine wall. Render only physically visible elements; a reverse view must not pull hidden furniture around a corner. Do not use any earlier S07 furnished image as a material authority. This S18 concept requires subsequent geometry, original-material, electrical and full-budget validation.

=== END PROMPT A902_S18A_LakeForestPlus_Cam_12_v1 ===

LATEST OWNER OVERRIDE AND ACTUAL INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is the exact existing Cam_12 view from the 17-style selector and is the EDIT TARGET: preserve its exact camera, architecture, floor, doors, kitchen footprint, countertop heights, dining location and ceiling. Do not follow the outdated INPUT ORDER above. Images 2 and 3 are the original Lake Forest material/furniture authority; image 4 is original hallway cabinet detailing; last image is the newly accepted S18A Cam02 for identical sofa, rug, coffee table, styling and material continuity in reverse view. The TV wall is behind camera; do not drag it into this image. Replace pale old-style wood, cloud sofa, pearl arcs and generic furnishings with the actual Lake Forest references. Fully dress with the same rug, throw, accessories and tailored full-height curtains wherever real windows are in frame. Keep the exact four/six chair count visible in target image, do not expand table. Make chair backs grey-brown wood and fine bronze sled bases with white woven seats; pale white dining top. Compact opal bead-strand dining light at existing pendant point, no new ceiling cove. On right central feature wall replace the old pale arc artwork with a single large framed panel of the original fine-veined brown stone with restrained brushed bronze edge. At the EXISTING visible corridor storage zone, show floor-to-ceiling practical closed cupboards with the original finely speckled greige fronts, slender bronze handles, serviceable door joints, preserving doorway and passage width. No invented cabinet through a structural wall. Bright readable luxury interior, neutral daytime fill plus 2700K warm furniture lighting, not an orange wash. Single landscape image, no text.
